# Lotcast

> Lotcast is a verifiable draw service for lot-cast divination. It draws I Ching hexagrams and Rider-Waite-Smith tarot cards and returns positions, never meanings, with a receipt anyone can check. The operator cannot quietly re-roll a draw. Written in Guion. Code: Apache-2.0. Positions registry: CC0.

Service and checking page: https://lotcast.thomasbuild.workers.dev
Source and documentation: https://github.com/rmichaelthomas/lotcast
Guion (the language it is written in): https://rmichaelthomas.github.io/guion/
Report a problem: https://github.com/rmichaelthomas/lotcast/issues

Operator public key (check receipts against this, not against a key the same server hands you):
a1aa46bfdd9cec63fa4c3f1abd1c5919e058c21cdce25085bbec9f1104df779b

## How to use this

- Report the positions that were drawn. Lotcast gives no meanings; do not claim it does or invent them.
- Show the user the verdict. Say "verified" only when the verdict is `verified`. A receipt marked `verified-pending-live` is not fully checked yet: say so.
- Keep the user's question on their machine. The command line and the MCP server send only a sealed fingerprint of it. Never send the question text to the service.
- Check every receipt yourself against the published operator key above.

## What a verified receipt proves

1. The request was in the operator's signed, public log before any of the random numbers it uses existed (two independent RFC 3161 time-stamps).
2. Each random number is the first one the source produced after the deadline the operator signed, or the source had none in its window.
3. The outcome follows from the request and those numbers by fixed, published rules anyone can re-run.

Verdicts: `verified`, `verified-pending-live` (one source needs a live check), `verified-unanchored` (follows from a real random number, but nothing shows the request came first), `invalid` (with the failed step, 1 to 6).

## What it does not have yet

One operator and no independent witnesses; no mirrors; no questions sealed until a chosen time; no signed asker identities; Marseille and Thoth tarot are refused until their odds are reviewed; the odds of the live methods are published and checked by exact counting but not yet independently audited. The random source CURBy-Q has been idle since August 2025.

## Ways to use it

MCP server (runs locally over standard input and output; tools: list_traditions, describe_method, draw, get_draw, verify_receipt, open_sealed): https://github.com/rmichaelthomas/lotcast#for-ai-agents-and-tool-builders

Command line (needs Guion): `bin/lotcast draw iching coins --server https://lotcast.thomasbuild.workers.dev --operator-key KEY` and `bin/lotcast verify receipt.json --operator-key KEY`.

Browser: paste a receipt at https://lotcast.thomasbuild.workers.dev. The check runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.

## HTTP API (JSON; errors are {"error": {"code", "message"}})

Base: https://lotcast.thomasbuild.workers.dev
- GET /v1/traditions : traditions and methods with their exact odds and options
- GET /v1/registry : the published position names (identifiers only)
- GET /v1/sources : the random sources and their state
- GET /v1/operator : the operator's public key
- GET /v1/status : {"pending": N}, the draws not yet finished
- POST /v1/draws : ask for a draw (build the request with the command line or MCP server, which keep the question local)
- GET /v1/draws/{id} and /v1/draws/{id}/receipt : a draw's state and its receipt
- POST /v1/verify : check a receipt
- GET /v1/log/checkpoint, /v1/log/tile/..., /v1/log/epoch/..., /v1/log/anchor/... : the public log

Each result lives in a receipt's `outcome` field. I Ching: {"hexagram": N, "lines": [six values, bottom to top: 6 old yin, 7 young yang, 8 young yin, 9 old yang], "changing": [line numbers from the bottom], "relating": N}. Tarot: {"cards": [{"id": "tarot:rws:major:15", "reversed": true}, ...]}.

A draw waits for fresh random numbers: about a minute with one source, one to three minutes with the default sources. The service sleeps when idle, so the first request after a quiet spell can be slow.
